topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and frames the scope and challenges of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide a foundational overview of the complement system's general architecture and core biochemical properties.

topics.label: Complement recognition and activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how distinct recognition pathways converge on cleaving and depositing C3 on pathogen surfaces to reach an activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream physiological mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates target pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells use regulatory proteins to prevent accidental complement activation and protect themselves from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations and disease vulnerabilities resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary mechanisms pathogens employ to evade and suppress complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
